subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the read-checkpoint race is repaired, should OpenClaw accept the new opt-in maintenance-timeout key and generic synchronous command-queue timeout callback as permanent supported contracts?
rationale: The bug and mechanical repair are clear, but adding operator configuration and a shared queue API requires maintainer ownership of long-term compatibility and semantics.

options.title: Accept after repair
options.body: Keep both contracts once deterministic coverage proves that persistence admitted before timeout remains behind the same-session read checkpoint.

options.title: Narrow the contracts
options.body: Use existing timeout policy and a context-engine-private lifecycle if maintainers do not want new permanent configuration and queue API surfaces.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Pause the PR if the canonical cancellation and transcript-persistence ownership model needs a broader design first.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair
recommendation.body: Keep both contracts once deterministic coverage proves that persistence admitted before timeout remains behind the same-session read checkpoint.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current deferred-maintenance checkpoint/livelock behavior and recently maintained the relevant queue timeout semantics.
